sources.title: Understanding Mechanical Behavior of Lunar Soils for the Study of Vehicle Mobility
sources.author: Heather Ann Oravec

sources.title: An Overview of Tire-Ground Contact Modeling Approaches for Surface Mobility Applications
Simulations of Mars Rover Traverses
sources.use: Equation 6 for the continuous rear stress mapping; equations 8-12 for stress location and shear. NASA's rendered rear z2 expression is malformed; the implementation follows Zhou equation 6 and tests zero endpoints/continuity.

assumptions: Rigid smooth cylindrical wheel. No compliance, tread, grousers, bulldozing, rear-wheel multipass, rate-dependent soil response or wheel rotational inertia.
Exit angle zero (no elastic soil rebound). Stress peak theta_m=(c1+c2*s)*theta_f. Sinkage solved from the full normal-force integral including tangential stress contribution.
Inclines use local-plane normal load mg*cos(alpha)/wheel_count and net demand mg*sin(alpha)/wheel_count; no independently calibrated slope-induced soil weakening or flow law.
Husky validation soil was prepared at 28-31% relative density, not this preset's 14%. Comparisons are preparation-transfer tests, not matched-soil validation.
Treating actual pneumatic/grouser wheels as rigid smooth cylinders is a proxy; it is not proven conservative.
Source pressure/sinkage/shear ranges are reported as transfer flags. The plate-to-wheel and speed/load transfer is exploratory, even when values fall inside these ranges.

numerical_domain.acceptance: Operating point requires slip strictly below 1; slip=1 evaluated only as the locked-wheel force limit

predeclared_benchmark_gate.scope: All six published Husky means, separate stock and rigid-wheel groups. No refit. Invalid/unreachable points are failures, not dropped successes.
predeclared_benchmark_gate.meaning: Exploratory accuracy gate only. Passing does not validate BP-1, our rover, or a 30-degree slope.

default_selection: Student selected rigid-wheel BWR as conservative design model, with 25 degree empty and 20 degree full slip<1 checks; no refitting and no change to published coefficients.
